name: Madhya Pradesh
summary_text: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no Madhya Pradesh-specific trans statute or enforcement series and records it among the states/UTs that have not constituted the mandated transgender welfare board; with national legal uniformity (no state criminalisation) the deviation was not material enough to score separately (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score.

sources.title: India’s Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill passed by parliament: removes self-identification, limits recognition to hijra/kinner and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and creates offences with up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender. National law applying uniformly in Madhya Pradesh; no state-specific findings in the piece.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: BBC report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment ending self-identification and mandating medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery, amid community and opposition protests; a Supreme Court-appointed advisory panel sought withdrawal and presidential assent is pending. Applies nationally including Madhya Pradesh; the article has no state angle.

Times of India (Kolkata edition, 18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged an RPF constable groped her in a "gender check" at Rabindra Sadan metro station; the RPF denied it and filed a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident, not a Madhya Pradesh one, kept as a national datapoint on security screening of gender-nonconforming people in public spaces.
